questions.q: What is the SI unit of power?
questions.solution:
Power is the rate of doing work; its SI unit is the watt (W).
1 watt = 1 joule per second.
**Answer: Watt**

questions.q: Which type of mirror is used as a rear-view mirror in vehicles?
questions.solution:
A convex mirror always gives an erect, diminished image and a wide field of view, ideal for seeing traffic behind.
**Answer: Convex mirror**

questions.q: Sound waves cannot travel through —
questions.solution:
Sound is a mechanical wave and needs a material medium to propagate.
There are no particles in a vacuum, so sound cannot travel through it.
**Answer: Vacuum**

questions.q: Which instrument is used to measure atmospheric pressure?
questions.solution:
A barometer measures atmospheric pressure.
A hygrometer measures humidity and an anemometer measures wind speed.
**Answer: Barometer**

questions.q: Which of the following is a non-renewable source of energy?
questions.solution:
Coal is a fossil fuel formed over millions of years and cannot be replenished quickly.
Solar, wind and tidal energy are renewable.
**Answer: Coal**

questions.q: The chemical formula of common salt is —
questions.solution:
Common salt is sodium chloride, NaCl.
NaOH is caustic soda; Na2CO3 is washing soda.
**Answer: NaCl**

questions.q: Which gas is known as laughing gas?
questions.solution:
Nitrous oxide (N2O), used as a mild anaesthetic, is called laughing gas.
**Answer: Nitrous oxide**
questions.shortcut: N2O = laughing gas; CO = carbon monoxide (poisonous).

questions.q: What is the pH value of a neutral solution at 25°C?
questions.solution:
A neutral solution has equal concentrations of H+ and OH− ions.
Its pH at 25°C is 7; below 7 is acidic and above 7 is basic.
**Answer: 7**

questions.q: Which is the lightest gas?
questions.solution:
Hydrogen is the lightest element and the lightest gas.
Helium is the second lightest.
**Answer: Hydrogen**

questions.q: Which vitamin is synthesised in the human body on exposure to sunlight?
questions.solution:
The skin produces vitamin D when exposed to the ultraviolet rays in sunlight.
**Answer: Vitamin D**

questions.q: Which cell organelle is called the powerhouse of the cell?
questions.solution:
Mitochondria release energy in the form of ATP during respiration.
Hence they are called the powerhouse of the cell.
**Answer: Mitochondria**

questions.q: Which blood group is regarded as the universal donor?
questions.solution:
Group O blood has neither A nor B antigens on its red cells, so it can be donated to persons of any blood group.
**Answer: O**
questions.shortcut: Universal donor = O; universal recipient = AB.

questions.q: Malaria is transmitted to humans by the bite of —
questions.solution:
Malaria is spread by the bite of the female Anopheles mosquito, which carries the Plasmodium parasite.
Aedes mosquitoes spread dengue.
**Answer: Female Anopheles mosquito**
questions.shortcut: Anopheles = malaria; Aedes = dengue; only females bite.

questions.q: Which is the largest gland in the human body?
questions.solution:
The liver is the largest gland and the largest internal organ of the human body.
**Answer: Liver**

questions.q: Who founded the Maurya Empire?
questions.solution:
Chandragupta Maurya, guided by Chanakya, founded the Maurya Empire around 322 BC.
Samudragupta belonged to the Gupta dynasty.
**Answer: Chandragupta Maurya**

questions.q: In which year was the Quit India Movement launched?
questions.solution:
Mahatma Gandhi launched the Quit India Movement in August 1942 with the call of 'Do or Die'.
**Answer: 1942**

questions.q: Who was the first Mughal emperor of India?
questions.solution:
Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi in the First Battle of Panipat (1526) and founded the Mughal dynasty.
**Answer: Babur**

questions.q: In which year did the Jallianwala Bagh massacre take place?
questions.solution:
General Dyer's troops fired on a peaceful gathering at Jallianwala Bagh, Amritsar, on 13 April 1919.
**Answer: 1919**

questions.q: Article 21 of the Constitution of India deals with —
options: Protection of life and personal liberty
questions.solution:
Article 21 says no person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except by procedure established by law.
Right to equality is Article 14.
**Answer: Protection of life and personal liberty**
questions.shortcut: Art. 14 = equality, Art. 19 = six freedoms, Art. 21 = life and liberty.

questions.q: Who is known as the Father of the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
Dr. B. R. Ambedkar chaired the Constitution's Drafting Committee and is called the Father of the Indian Constitution.
**Answer: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar**

questions.q: The President of India is elected by —
options: Elected members of both Houses of Parliament and elected members of State Legislative Assemblies
All members of both Houses of Parliament
All members of Parliament and all members of State Legislative Assemblies
questions.solution:
The President is elected indirectly by an electoral college of elected MPs of both Houses and elected members of the State Legislative Assemblies.
Nominated members and MLCs do not vote.
**Answer: Elected members of Parliament and State Legislative Assemblies**
questions.shortcut: Key word: ELECTED members only — never nominated members or MLCs.

questions.q: Which is the longest river of India?
questions.solution:
The Ganga, about 2,525 km long within India, is the longest river of the country.
**Answer: Ganga**

questions.q: The Tropic of Cancer passes through how many Indian states?
questions.solution:
It passes through Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura and Mizoram — 8 states.
**Answer: 8**
questions.shortcut: Mnemonic: Gu-RaM-CJ-TM (Gujarat, Rajasthan, MP, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, WB, Tripura, Mizoram).

questions.q: Which is the highest mountain peak located entirely within India?
questions.solution:
Kangchenjunga (8,586 m) in Sikkim is the highest peak located entirely in India.
Everest is in Nepal and K2 lies in Pakistan-occupied territory.
**Answer: Kangchenjunga**

questions.q: Which Indian state has the longest coastline?
questions.solution:
Gujarat has the longest coastline among Indian states, about 1,600 km.
**Answer: Gujarat**

questions.q: In India, the repo rate is decided by —
questions.solution:
The repo rate, at which the RBI lends short-term funds to banks, is decided by the RBI's Monetary Policy Committee.
**Answer: Reserve Bank of India**

questions.q: NITI Aayog replaced which of the following bodies?
questions.solution:
NITI Aayog was set up on 1 January 2015 in place of the Planning Commission.
**Answer: Planning Commission**

questions.q: Bharatanatyam is a classical dance form of which state?
questions.solution:
Bharatanatyam developed in the temples of Tamil Nadu.
Kathakali and Mohiniyattam belong to Kerala.
**Answer: Tamil Nadu**

questions.q: Which river is known as the 'Sorrow of Bihar'?
questions.solution:
The Kosi frequently changes course and floods large parts of Bihar, hence 'Sorrow of Bihar'.
The Damodar is the 'Sorrow of Bengal'.
**Answer: Kosi**
questions.shortcut: Kosi = Sorrow of Bihar; Damodar = Sorrow of Bengal.

questions.q: The Dronacharya Award is given to —
questions.solution:
The Dronacharya Award honours eminent coaches who have produced medal winners in international events.
The Arjuna Award goes to outstanding sportspersons.
**Answer: Eminent sports coaches**
questions.shortcut: Dronacharya (the guru) = coaches; Arjuna (the archer) = players.

questions.q: Who wrote the book 'The Discovery of India'?
questions.solution:
Jawaharlal Nehru wrote 'The Discovery of India' during his imprisonment at Ahmednagar fort (1942-46).
**Answer: Jawaharlal Nehru**

questions.q: Which city is known as the 'Pink City' of India?
questions.solution:
Jaipur is called the Pink City because of the pink colour of its historic buildings.
**Answer: Jaipur**

questions.q: In which of the following fields is the Nobel Prize NOT awarded?
questions.solution:
Nobel Prizes are awarded in Physics, Chemistry, Medicine, Literature, Peace and Economics.
There is no Nobel Prize for Mathematics.
**Answer: Mathematics**

questions.q: How many vacancies were notified in the RRB NTPC 2026 cycle (CEN 06/2026 and CEN 07/2026 taken together)?
questions.solution:
The 2026 short notices list 3,477 graduate (CEN 06/2026) and 1,688 undergraduate (CEN 07/2026) posts.
Together = 5,165. (8,868 was the total of the 2025 cycle.)
**Answer: 5,165**

questions.q: The short notice for RRB NTPC CEN 06/2026 and CEN 07/2026 was released on —
questions.solution:
RRB released the short notices for the 2026 NTPC cycle on 21 September 2026.
8 October 2026 is the tentative opening date of graduate applications.
**Answer: 21 September 2026**

questions.q: RRB NTPC CBT 1 consists of how many questions and what duration?
questions.solution:
CBT 1 has 100 questions — Mathematics 30, Reasoning 30, General Awareness 40 — in a single 90-minute block.
(CBT 2 has 120 questions in 90 minutes.)
**Answer: 100 questions in 90 minutes**

questions.q: CBT 1 of RRB NTPC is conducted for what purpose?
options: To select candidates for appointment directly
To prepare the final merit list
questions.solution:
CBT 1 is only a screening stage — it shortlists candidates for CBT 2, and its marks do not count in the final merit.
**Answer: To shortlist candidates for CBT 2**

questions.q: What is the marking scheme of RRB NTPC CBT 1?
options: 1/3 mark is deducted for each wrong answer
1/4 mark is deducted for each wrong answer
1/2 mark is deducted for each wrong answer
questions.solution:
Each correct answer earns 1 mark and each wrong answer costs 1/3 mark; unattempted questions carry no penalty.
**Answer: 1/3 mark is deducted for each wrong answer**

questions.q: Which of the following is the National Song of India?
questions.solution:
'Vande Mataram', composed by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay, is the National Song of India.
'Jana Gana Mana' is the National Anthem.
**Answer: Vande Mataram**
questions.shortcut: Song = Vande Mataram; Anthem = Jana Gana Mana.

questions.q: The Statue of Unity, the world's tallest statue, is located in which state?
questions.solution:
The Statue of Unity, honouring Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, stands at Kevadia in Gujarat near the Sardar Sarovar Dam.
**Answer: Gujarat**
